cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3 ('Fair... the log comes first'); T6 takes up T5's patch test.
cells.limitation: T3 skips T2's bare-minimum routine and opens a separate thread.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T8's tingling-versus-lingering-burn distinction, absent from openings, drives T10 and section E.
cells.limitation: T11 summarises the plan rather than adding a distinction.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T8-T10 examine caution versus experimentation over whether sensation means harm.
cells.limitation: T11 names whether testing a fading sting is worth it, then leaves it unexamined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T4 widens the method after T3; T7 adds a pair stage after T6.
cells.limitation: The Bias Watcher's own position is never reshaped by the others.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T11 gives the plan a shape and names the remaining disagreement.
cells.limitation: The open question at T11 is named but not sharpened with any criterion.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T6 states the patch-test case fairly before attacking its site and timing.
cells.limitation: T9 attacks treating every sensation as damage; T8 had already excluded brief tingling.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T6 names the forearm-equals-face assumption and the false all-clear; T7 answers with pair testing.
cells.limitation: T5's point that relief proves nothing is never answered by the Logician.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T7's acids-plus-retinoid interaction and T6's delayed reactions are accurate general claims.
cells.limitation: T9's expectation-amplifies-sensation point sits loosely on the Kahneman basis; unverified.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T7 labels the pair stage 'my extension, not a claim that Mill wrote about skincare.'
cells.limitation: T3 predicts the user will pick the scariest ingredient list as if certain.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4 concedes T3's log; T7 concedes T6's layering trap and extends the method.
cells.limitation: T10's 'narrowing' repeats T8's own distinction, so the revision is staged.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames the concern as isolating one cause among three simultaneous changes.
cells.limitation: Whether the user needs the culprit named or simply relief is never distinguished.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 and section A build the method on three products changed at once.
cells.limitation: The one-week timeline never informs how quickly a reaction should appear or fade.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E's first branch keeps the user's goal of isolating the cause.
cells.limitation: T2's bare-minimum routine reflects the Subtractor's preference, not a stated user priority.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 sets a stopping ceiling; section E names urgent care for breathing trouble or swelling.
cells.limitation: T2 assumes an 'already angry face' though severity is unknown.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on severity, response to pausing, and combination effects.
cells.limitation: No mind asks what the three products contain, a consequential lead never branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D asks when the user would rather stop and see a professional.
cells.limitation: No alternative motives offered: keeping the routine, reassurance, or avoiding a doctor.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T5 and T6 expose the assumptions that relief or a clean patch is a verdict.
cells.limitation: Assumptions examined are mostly about method; the user's own beliefs appear only at T3.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 weighs a bad reaction's large downside against one more serum's small upside.
cells.limitation: T11's worth-the-effort question is never weighed against what the user values.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T9 notes expectation can amplify sensation without pathologising the user.
cells.limitation: Sunk cost of three purchases or hope the new routine works is never raised.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E's conditional branches let the user apply their own observations.
cells.limitation: Most turns instruct; section D holds the only question the user can answer.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Options span pausing, stripping down, staged reintroduction, pair tests, patch tests, professional care.
cells.limitation: Simply waiting it out (T11) is never laid out as an option with consequences.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T5 and T6 give the patch test's costs: wrong skin, delayed reactions.
cells.limitation: T2 calls pausing nearly costless; weeks of staged reintroduction are never counted.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: fades within minutes, lingers between applications, returns only combined, each with its option.
cells.limitation: T1's 'few days apart' and T4's 'clean week' are not derived from user facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A singles out severity and response to pausing as the decisive unknowns.
cells.limitation: T3's list weighs detergent, wind and shaving equally, not by likelihood.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T11: record changes, pause non-essentials, wait for calm, reintroduce one at a time.
cells.limitation: 'Wait until the skin is calm' (T11) gives no sign of when calm is reached.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: Plain wording throughout, e.g. T8's 'brief tingling that fades within minutes is one thing.'
cells.limitation: T5's 'damaged barrier' goes unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6's 'A patch test has its own trap' points unambiguously to T5.
cells.limitation: T11's 'what we still disagree about' traces to no turn arguing the opposite.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within the word range, each carrying one move.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Positions stay distinct: method, bias, removal; T10 states its change explicitly.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one measured register at near-equal length; T2 calls a mind 'Mill.'

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Little repetition; T11's recap feeds the synthesis.
cells.limitation: T10 largely restates T8's severity line; section D repeats T11.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T8 sets real stakes: lingering burn, swelling or hives versus one more serum.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay generic; the user's actual severity never becomes the point of contention.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T9's Bias Watcher turns against caution, an unexpected move from the skeptic.
cells.limitation: T10's reversal repeats T8's distinction; T9 supplied no new argument to cause it.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: The Subtractor's 'already angry face' and 'where the real risk lives' give some edge.
cells.limitation: Expression is flat across minds; little personality beyond each stated stance.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T4: 'Stripping down isn't just relief, it's already an experiment.'
cells.limitation: No vivid analogy or concrete example beyond generic product scenarios.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T9's pushback shifts direction after several turns of caution.
cells.limitation: Uniform measured rhythm across eleven turns; little emotional movement or build.

strengths: T7 extends one-at-a-time testing into pair testing as a direct answer to T6's layering trap.
Section E branches on observable signs (fading within minutes, lingering, calming after a pause) with the option each favours.
T5 and T6 expose two false verdicts: relief after pausing and a clean patch test.
weaknesses: No mind asks what the three products contain (T1-T11), leaving the most direct lead unused.
T9 misreads T8 as treating every sensation as harm, so T10's narrowing restates T8 rather than reversing.
All three minds share one measured register and near-equal turn lengths, flattening voice and rhythm.

symptoms.observed: Never asks what the three products contain, though actives like acids or retinoids are main leads.
symptoms.evidence: probably the product with the scariest ingredient list

symptoms.observed: T9 attacks treating every sensation as damage; T8 had already excluded brief tingling.
symptoms.evidence: If every sensation counts as damage, nobody ever tries anything.

symptoms.observed: T10's narrowing repeats T8's own distinction, so the reversal has no new cause.
symptoms.evidence: I'll narrow my claim, then. Mild, short-lived tingling right after application

symptoms.observed: Never distinguishes what the user wants: keep the products, stop the sting, or avoid a doctor.
symptoms.evidence: whether the whole process is worth it if the sting simply fades

symptoms.observed: Pausing called nearly costless; weeks of staged single and pair reintroduction never counted.
symptoms.evidence: Pausing is a safe move because it costs almost nothing.

findings.location: B. MINDS and all basis fields
findings.description: Attributions to Mill, Kahneman and Taleb fit their known themes but cannot be verified; no source evidence attached.
Expectation amplifying sensation is a nocebo idea only loosely tied to the Thinking, Fast and Slow basis.

rubric_fit_notes: Criterion 4 fits a skincare troubleshooting question weakly: desires, fears and outside expectations matter less than diagnostic method, so low C4 ratings partly reflect the rubric rather than a debate failure. Medical accuracy judged from general knowledge only.
question_type_note: Read as a decision (troubleshooting) question, so every cell was read as written, with criterion 5 centred on how to isolate the cause and when to stop testing.
